subtopic: Small Account Balances and Fee Erosion
source_evidence: for investment advisory accounts with lower balances, small monthly fees like these can add up to a large percentage of the amount invested
question: Why can a subscription-based advisory fee have a greater impact on a small account than on a larger one?
answer: A subscription fee is a set recurring amount, so it can represent a larger share of a small balance. For example, the source explains that a $3 monthly fee on a $500 account totals $36 per year, which is more than 7% of the account’s value. Fees can also reduce the balance over time, making them a larger percentage of the remaining money.
formula_latex: \text{Annual fee as a percentage of account balance}=\frac{\text{monthly fee}\times 12}{\text{account balance}}\times 100\%
